title: Derived composition for an open-pushforward-acyclic module
statement: Let f:X → Y be a scheme morphism and W an open subscheme of X with inclusion j. Assume the module categories on X and W have injective resolutions. If M is an O_W-module acyclic for j_*, then for every natural number q there is an isomorphism R^q f_*(j_*M) ≅ R^q(f j)_*M. No affine, separatedness or quasi-coherence assumption is required.

source.place: Functor.quasiIso_map_of_rightAcyclic_nat and Functor.rightDerivedObjIsoOfResolution; injective-resolution proof of the comparison in blueprint lem-pc-cech-resolution, paragraphs 2 and 3

proof.text: Restriction to W preserves monomorphisms, as its maps on sections are the original maps on the image open. The restriction adjunction therefore sends injectives under j_* to injectives, by Mathlib Adjunction.map_injective. Both j_* and f_* are left exact by their adjunctions.

Choose an injective resolution I of M. Every term is j_*-acyclic. The single complex on M also has j_*-acyclic terms by hM and the vanishing of its positive terms. Functor.quasiIso_map_of_rightAcyclic_nat therefore makes the induced augmentation j_*M to j_*I a quasi-isomorphism.

Apply Functor.rightDerivedObjIsoOfResolution to f_* and the augmentation j_*M to j_*I; the terms are injective and hence f_*-acyclic. Pushforward composition identifies f_*j_*I with (f j)_*I. Compose its homology isomorphism with the inverse of InjectiveResolution.isoRightDerivedObj for (f j)_*.

lean.statement:
theorem open_pushforward_rightDerived_comparison
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [HasInjectiveResolutions (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    (W : X.Opens) [HasInjectiveResolutions W.toScheme.Modules]
    (M : W.toScheme.Modules)
    (hM : (Scheme.Modules.pushforward W.ι).rightAcyclic M) (q : ℕ) :
    Nonempty
      (((RingedSpace.moduleDirectImage f.toLRSHom.toShHom).rightDerived q).obj
          ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward W.ι).obj M) ≅
        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (W.ι ≫ f)).rightDerived q).obj M)
